w10_T4_000748: Marcus started with 12 apples from his garden. He multiplied his collection by gathering 6 times as many more. Then he gave 20 to his neighbors. He doubled what remained by careful counting. Finally, he donated 55 to a local shelter. His uncle had given him 3 extra apples last week. How many apples does Marcus have at the end?
w10_T4_000749: A bakery had 114 loaves in stock this morning. By afternoon, production tripled the amount. In the evening, they sold 166 loaves. The remaining loaves were made into 6 large orders. When divided among 4 shops equally, each shop received their share. The first shop then added 78 loaves from their storage room. They received 26 new orders to fulfill. A competitor had opened with 200 products. How many loaves did the first shop have after all changes?
w10_T4_000751: A library shelf started with 34 books in the morning. By midday, 16 were checked out by students. Then 63 books were returned by patrons. During the afternoon, 17 books were sent to be repaired. By evening, donations added 20 new books. The librarian doubled the shelf count to prepare for the week. Finally, 69 more books arrived from the warehouse. How many books were on the shelf at the end of the day?
w10_T4_000754: A farmer had 33 chickens on Monday morning. He doubled his flock. A week later, he multiplied it by 8. He then added 71 chickens from a neighbor's farm. He decided to organize them by doubling one section. That doubled section was then halved for safety. At year end, he multiplied all chickens by 6 for breeding season. He had purchased 20 chickens the previous year. How many chickens did the farmer have in total?
w10_T4_000757: A soccer team had 103 training passes to work with. They multiplied passes by 9 for advanced drills. They then tripled that set for 7 different practice sessions. The coach added 11 cones to mark zones. He then multiplied the zones by 9 for expansion. Finally, 21 additional cones arrived for setup. The field had cost 500 dollars to prepare. How many training resources did the team have?
w10_T4_000762: A warehouse held 214 boxes initially. They shipped out 170 boxes to stores. The remaining stock was packaged into 6 containers. Each container held items worth adding 80 more units to the total value. That value was multiplied by 5 for the grand total. Finally, 1355 boxes were removed for clearance. A new manager had joined the team 3 months prior. How many boxes remained in the warehouse?
w10_T4_000781: A gardener planted 59 tomato seeds initially. He multiplied his planting by 9 to expand the garden. He doubled the rows for better organization. He then added 73 saplings he'd grown elsewhere. He removed 47 damaged seedlings from the garden. David had helped plant 30 seedlings last season. How many healthy plants did the gardener have?
w10_T4_000787: A bank account started with 168 dollars. A withdrawal of 105 was made for expenses. The remaining balance was then multiplied by 4 through an investment. Then 47 dollars in interest was added. That sum was multiplied by 5 for monthly compounding. The entire amount was multiplied by 8 for quarterly calculations. The customer had deposited money 6 times last year. What was the final account balance?
w10_T4_000790: A shop sold 208 items in the first week. It sold 205 items the second week. They added 6 items to inventory. Then added 20 more items. They added 28 items from a new shipment. Converting to dozen lots showed the final count. The store manager worked 8 days that month. How many items did the shop have total?
w10_T4_000796: A factory produced 185 units Monday. They multiplied production by 8 for the Tuesday shift. They multiplied again by 8 for Wednesday. They added 45 units from returns. They subtracted 3481 defective units. The remainder was multiplied by 6 for new packaging. Then 25 bonus units were added. A different factory made 60 units. How many final units did this factory have?
w10_T4_000799: A student started with 60 marbles. She removed 40 during a game with friends. She gained 53 marbles from winning trades. She multiplied her collection by 8 through careful organization. She then split them equally in half with her brother. Marcus had 30 marbles of his own. How many marbles did the student end up with?
w10_T4_000801: A baker had 144 pastries to sell. He removed 22 that burned in the oven. He removed 17 more that didn't rise properly. He multiplied his good pastries by 4 for the afternoon rush order. He added 4 to the count for last-minute fresh bakes. The bakery used 8 dozen eggs that day. How many pastries did he have ready to sell?
w10_T4_000802: A print shop received 211 pages of orders Monday. They multiplied the order by 7 times for the week. They shipped 192 pages to a major client. They then multiplied the rest by 9 for rush processing. They multiplied again by 8 for bulk package sizing. They added 28 bonus pages for customer loyalty. The office building used 50 pages of paper daily. How many total pages did the shop process?
w10_T4_000803: A concert venue started with 59 tickets. They multiplied available seats by 9 for the first show. They added 40 more premium seats. They multiplied the total by 7 for a second event. They multiplied again by 8 for the full season pass. The parking lot held 100 cars. How many tickets did the venue sell total?
w10_T4_000805: A collector had 116 coins on Monday. He tripled his collection through purchases. He added 42 rare coins on Wednesday. He added 29 more coins from an auction. He added 61 vintage coins to complete a set. He had given away 25 coins to a friend last month. How many coins did the collector have in total?
w10_T4_000812: A restaurant served 232 meals on opening day. They removed 133 from the counter for catering. They multiplied the remaining meals by 3 for weekend prep. They multiplied by 2 for holiday events. They added 68 meals from new menu items. They added 71 pre-ordered meals to the kitchen. They had planned to serve 500 customers this month. How many total meals were prepared?
w10_T4_000814: A coach had 97 basketballs initially. He multiplied the supply by 4 through donations. He removed 278 old balls for recycling. He added 75 new balls from inventory. He doubled the final count for tournament preparation. The gym budget was 2000 dollars. How many basketballs did the coach have ready?
w10_T4_000818: A farmer started with 152 apple trees. He added 23 new saplings to his orchard. He multiplied the rows by 7 for organization. He multiplied by 2 for split shifting work. He multiplied by 8 for seasonal expansion plans. He owned 5 other orchards across town. How many apple trees did the farmer manage in this location?
w10_T4_000819: A fund began with 136 dollars donated. Contributors added 14 dollars to support the cause. A donor added 69 more dollars generously. Another gift of 14 dollars arrived. The total was multiplied by 9 through grant matching. The funds were then multiplied by 8 for reinvestment. The organization had 10 staff members. How much money did the fund have?
w10_T4_000828: A store started with 76 toys in inventory. They multiplied stock by 9 for restocking. They added 64 toys from a supplier delivery. They added 35 more toys in the evening. They added 22 toys from returns. They removed 622 toy units for a recall. The store manager worked 40 hours a week. How many toys remained on the shelves?
w10_T4_000829: A publisher had 194 books printed. They added 13 copies for author events. They multiplied the total by 5 for book club orders. They removed 21 damaged copies. They multiplied by 6 for regional distribution. They removed 745 books for clearance sales. The print run cost 3000 dollars. How many books did the publisher have left?
w10_T4_000832: A museum had 75 artifacts on display initially. They added 77 new pieces to a collection. They removed 25 for conservation cleaning. They removed 99 more pieces temporarily. They added back 65 restored pieces. The facility opened to the public 6 days a week. How many artifacts were on display at the end?
w10_T4_000833: A trainer had 112 hours of classes scheduled. He doubled the schedule for expansion. He added 75 new student hours to the calendar. He doubled again for summer camps. He multiplied by 7 for weekend workshops. He added 52 hours from evening sessions. He added 61 emergency tutoring hours. The gym charged 25 dollars per hour. How many total training hours did he schedule?
w10_T4_000835: A charity had 64 boxes of supplies to distribute. They split the boxes equally among 4 communities. They again split equally among 4 homes per community. They multiplied by 7 to account for family sizes. They multiplied by 3 for donation drives. They added 19 emergency boxes. They had 100 volunteers. How many supply boxes were distributed?
w10_T4_000838: A hotel had 140 rooms initially. They added 16 new suites from expansion. They divided rooms equally among 4 floors for management. Each floor multiplied its allocation by 7. They subtracted 253 rooms for maintenance. They added 39 newly renovated rooms. They had 200 employees total. How many rooms were available to rent?
